title: Pattern kinds
hook: A ragged CSV import row is a list pattern problem; an LTI launch payload is a property pattern problem. Name the kind, then write the arm.

sections.heading: Declaration, type, constant, relational, logical
sections.prose: A declaration pattern (seq is IList<T> list) tests type and assigns. Type patterns without a name still reject null. Constant patterns match values, including null. Relational patterns use <, >, <=, >= against constants. Logical patterns combine with and, or, not — not &&. is not null is the idiomatic null test that ignores overloaded ==. Parentheses group relational ranges: (> 32) and (< 212).

snippets.label: Relational bands on an attempt score
snippets.explanation: Order matters. After < 50, < 70 only sees 50–69. The or arm rejects impossible percents before bands run.

sections.heading: Property, positional, list
sections.prose: Property patterns match { Name: pattern, Nested: { } }. { } by itself is any non-null. Positional patterns call Deconstruct, which records get for free. List patterns match arrays and other countable sequences: [first, second], [_, "WITHDRAWAL", .., var amount], [.., var last]. Slice .. consumes zero or more elements. This is the CSV import story: columns shift, the last field is still the amount.

snippets.label: List pattern on a CSV row
snippets.explanation: WITHDRAWAL rows have a variable number of middle columns. .. skips them. The var pattern binds the last cell. Microsoft’s pattern-matching overview uses this shape on bank CSV; bulk exam CSV is the same idea.

interviewTakeaways: Declaration patterns introduce a variable only on the success path.
Relational + and/or/not express ranges; order of switch arms is semantic.
Property patterns match records without Deconstruct; positional patterns need it.
List patterns plus .. are for sequences whose shape varies, such as CSV.
commonPitfalls: Writing && inside a pattern instead of and.
Matching [a, b] on an IEnumerable that is not a list — list patterns need a countable indexer sequence.
Using var x as a catch-all before more specific arms, making them unreachable.

jsTsCorrelations.note: const [_, kind, ...rest] = row is runtime destructuring. C# list patterns are compile-checked matches that can fail to the next arm. JS destructuring throws or yields undefined.
